name: Kokoro-FastAPI
description: OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech API server wrapping the Kokoro-82M model. Dockerized FastAPI/uvicorn application exposing /v1/audio/speech and /v1/audio/voices on port 8880 with 50+ voices across 9 languages, streaming audio, voice mixing, and word-level timestamped captions. No authentication by default.
auth_notes: remsky/Kokoro-FastAPI (primary project): zero authentication by default. The OpenAI client api_key field is documented as 'not-needed' — any non-empty placeholder satisfies the client library, no server-side check occurs. Auth is entirely opt-in and must be enforced externally via reverse proxy; no built-in API key middleware in the main image. hwdsl2/kokoro-server variant adds optional KOKORO_API_KEY via environment variable: fresh installs auto-generate a key only when /var/lib/kokoro volume is mounted; existing installs without a key remain fully open for backward compatibility. Neither image enforces HTTPS natively. No rate limiting is implemented in either variant. The /docs (Swagger UI), /v1/audio/voices, and /health endpoints are universally unauthenticated even in deployments that have partially configured auth.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Title or body match on canonical port 8880; surfaces instances using default docker-compose port binding
Conjunctive match on default voice name and voices JSON key returned by unauthenticated GET /v1/audio/voices — high-specificity body signal
Web UI title combined with FastAPI default server header and canonical port — filters to FastAPI-stack Kokoro deployments
Version string in HTML/API response body; useful for scoping CVE applicability to specific release bands
OpenAI-compat endpoint path in HTML body combined with uvicorn server header; catches instances where title is customized

known_vulns: CVE-2026-48710: Starlette < 1.0.1 reconstructs request.url from an unvalidated HTTP Host header, enabling routing/middleware security bypass (CVSS 6.5 Medium, NVD). Applicable — Kokoro-FastAPI runs on Starlette; verify the pinned Starlette version before scoring.
No built-in authentication — POST /v1/audio/speech accepts unauthenticated synthesis requests from any source; open TTS compute at operator cost (no default API-key check).
No rate limiting by default — automated request floods exhaust CPU/GPU and host resources.
FastAPI /docs and /openapi.json enabled by default — full API schema disclosure aids endpoint enumeration.
risk_notes: Primary unauth risk is compute theft: TTS synthesis is CPU/GPU-intensive and billed per inference on cloud deployments; an unauthenticated instance can be weaponized to exhaust GPU/CPU budget at no cost to the attacker. Secondary risk is deepfake audio production: the 50+ multilingual voices with voice-mixing and phoneme-level control enable synthesis of convincing impersonation audio for vishing/fraud campaigns. /dev/captioned_speech exposes word-level timestamps that aid audio forensics evasion. The /docs Swagger UI is universally unauth and enumerates the full API surface including dev endpoints. No rate limiting means resource exhaustion DoS is trivially achievable. The /dev/phonemize endpoint exfiltrates phoneme representations of arbitrary input text — low-sensitivity in isolation but useful for probing model internals. Audio responses are served in multiple formats (MP3/WAV/FLAC/Opus/M4A/PCM) enabling direct exfiltration of synthesized content. DigitalOcean and Railway deployments are commonly exposed directly on public IPs per documented integration guides.
deployment_notes: Default docker-compose.yml binds to 0.0.0.0:8880:8880, making the TTS API internet-facing unless explicitly changed to 127.0.0.1:8880:8880. GPU variant uses NVIDIA CUDA; CPU variant uses ONNX runtime — both expose identical API surface. Documented deployment targets include Railway, Dokploy, DigitalOcean, Synology NAS, RunPod serverless, and Spheron GPU cloud. No HTTPS is provided by the container itself; docs recommend a reverse proxy for TLS termination. Versions in production range from v0.1.4 through v0.5.0 (v0.5.0 is the current release as of 2026-06). ONNX threading tunable via env (ONNX_NUM_THREADS, ONNX_INTER_OP_THREADS). Open WebUI integration is widely documented and common — instances may appear fronted behind Open WebUI rather than directly exposed.
